newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo Bank to securitise 800 bln yen in loans.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Bank to securitise 800 bln yen in loans.

text.p: Sumitomo Bank Ltd said on Tuesday that it would securitise 800 billion yen worth of corporate loans by the end of March 1998 in a bid to strengthen its financial status.
The bank plans to first issue asset-backed securities worth about 200 billion yen as early as next month through special purpose companies established in the Cayman Islands.
The units would sell medium-term euro notes and samurai yen commercial paper to investors and deposit the funds financed by the securities at Sumitomo Bank.
Depositing the funds at the bank means the securities will earn a higher debt rating, the bank said.
The bank added that the plan will enable it to carry out a large-scale reduction of its risk assets.

The bank said it expects that by securitising 800 billion yen worth of its loans it would be able to raise its capital-adequacy ratio, required by the Bank for International Settlements for banks operating internationally, by 0.1 to 0.2 percentage point.
The bank had a capital-adequacy ratio of 8.75 percent at the end of March.
